clue.text: HQ for high-fliers in capital concerned with recruiting graduates

parts.note: capital as an adjective means excellent, first-rate, which is A1, written AI

indicators.note: recruiting means taking members in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: RE is the Latin-derived word meaning about, concerning
BAs are Bachelors of Arts, university graduates

explanation.surface: A headquarters for top executives in a capital city that is busy hiring new graduates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is not a city but the adjective meaning excellent, as A1 is; 'recruiting' signals that the graduates go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An installation from which military aircraft operate is the headquarters for pilots, who are literally high-fliers.

clue.text: Parisian appreciated a piece of England, as it were

definitions.text: piece of England, as it were

parts.note: a Parisian showing appreciation says merci, French for thank you

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's grateful remark about a chunk of English territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it were' allows for the fact that this region was once a kingdom rather than a modern part of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical identity: an Anglo-Saxon kingdom covering the English Midlands, now just a regional name.

clue.text: Rabbits on picture from the 1970s

definitions.meaning: to rabbit on is British slang for talking at tedious length, also called to jaw

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: chatters endlessly, and the title of Spielberg's 1975 thriller about a great white shark.

clue.text: Face letter from abroad — the last letter

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a foreign letter
Z ends the English alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone faces a letter from overseas, the final one they will receive.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang, short for physiognomy, meaning someone's face or expression.

clue.text: Can be wiped off in time with artist's brush

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a fine paintbrush is made of sable hair and called a sable

explanation.surface: Paint that can be removed in time with a painter's brush.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for something that can be rubbed out or removed, like a pencil mark.

clue.text: Attack from sheep in one's compound

indicators.note: in places the sheep word inside the rearranged letters
compound means mixed together, so the letters of the word one's are rearranged

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: An assault launched from the sheep kept in someone's farmyard enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a farmyard enclosure but is the mixing signal, giving SEON; 'in' places the ram inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb meaning to assail or attack someone suddenly.

clue.text: Some trace distance, having returned vehicle

indicators.note: having returned means the run of letters is read backwards
some of the words trace distance supply a run of their letters

explanation.surface: Someone has traced part of the distance after bringing back a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes RACEDIS from 'trace distance'; 'having returned' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A small car attached to the side of a motorcycle for a passenger; also a cocktail, as are many answers here.

clue.text: Actress's quiet line delivered in Irish place of worship

indicators.note: delivered in tells us the line piece arrives in place next to the Irish abbreviation

parts.note: sh is the command for quiet
a ley is a straight line linking ancient landmarks
a temple is a building for worship

explanation.surface: An actor's softly spoken line given in an Irish church.
explanation.walkthrough: A ley line is a supposed alignment of ancient sites.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollywood's most famous child star of the 1930s, later a US diplomat; also a non-alcoholic cocktail.

clue.text: Heather, grabbing one pound, is converting into cash

indicators.note: grabbing means the plant word holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: ling is another name for common heather
one is the Roman numeral I
a quid is British slang for a pound sterling
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Heather pockets a pound while selling things off for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a name; it is the plant LING. QUID is British slang for a pound coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning assets into ready money is the financial sense of making them liquid.

clue.text: Eurovision band — 4 vocalised with brass accompaniment

indicators.note: with places the money piece alongside the spoken piece

parts.note: brass is British slang for money, as is bucks

indicators.note: vocalised means the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: 4 refers to the answer at 4-down, a slang word for face

explanation.surface: A pop group singing the fourth number accompanied by a brass section.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' points to 4-down's answer, PHIZ, which said aloud sounds like FIZZ.
explanation.definitionFit: The British pop group won the 1981 Eurovision Song Contest; the name is also a champagne cocktail.

clue.text: Love uniform when in senior rank

indicators.note: when in tells us the pieces go inside the senior abbreviation

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Affection for one's uniform on reaching high military rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like a military grade but is the adjective meaning foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank as an adjective means rancid or gone off, as sour milk is.

clue.text: Infection appears when rusty nail catches fellow at university

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as he arrived

indicators.note: catches means the reworked letters take the fellow abbreviation inside
rusty means corroded or out of shape, so the letters of nail are reworked

explanation.surface: An infection develops when a rusty nail scratches a university fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rusty' rearranges NAIL into IANL, which 'catches' F. 'Rusty Nail' is also a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of an influenza pandemic, notably that of 1957, so a kind of infection.

clue.text: Father's seen before brother

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A priest is seen ahead of a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: French for brother, also used for a friar.

clue.text: Outlaw keeping old relative in line

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: Ry is the abbreviation for railway, a line
bro is short for brother, a relative

explanation.surface: An outlaw keeps an aged family member in check.
explanation.walkthrough: A railway line, abbreviated RY, holds O and BRO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish folk hero and outlaw immortalised by Walter Scott; also a whisky cocktail.

clue.text: Short animal welcome on rug? In principle, not at all

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the greeting piece after the first piece
in principle, read as the principal or first letter, picks the opening letter of rug

parts.note: hi is a word of welcome
no means not at all

explanation.surface: A welcome mat that, in theory, never welcomes anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In principle' puns on 'principal': the first letter of 'rug', R.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipped form of rhinoceros, so the animal's name in short.

clue.text: Guard software tool

parts.note: screw is slang for a prison guard
a driver is a piece of software that controls a device

explanation.surface: A prison guard uses a piece of computer software.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand tool for turning screws; also a vodka and orange cocktail.

clue.text: Ballerina's leap better, as one's in character

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it

indicators.note: in puts the one inside the character piece

parts.note: a role is a character played on stage
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A dancer's jump is improved, as she is playing a part.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap in ballet (and in dressage) where the legs are kicked out, from the Italian for a goat's leap.

clue.text: Couple who oppose lay spiritualist of late

parts.note: North and East are opponents at the bridge table
to lay money is to bet, to wager

explanation.surface: A couple who oppose a lay preacher who has recently turned to spiritualism.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South play against East-West, so N and E sit on opposing sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Follower of the modern alternative movement of holistic and spiritual beliefs, a recent kind of spiritual seeker.

clue.text: Perhaps sharks, from tail to head, of narrow build

indicators.note: from tail to head means the last letter is moved to the front

parts.note: loan sharks are an example of moneylenders

explanation.surface: Sharks, from tail to snout, have a slim build.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from tail to head' moves the final S of LENDERS to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Slim or slight in figure, as of a narrow frame.

clue.text: See 8
Missile regularly sent that hurt delicate part of body

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of sent is taken

parts.note: ow is the cry of something that hurt
a ball is a delicate part of a man's body

explanation.surface: A thrown object was sent and struck someone in a sensitive spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes S and N from 'sent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed ball of snow thrown in play is a winter missile; also an advocaat cocktail.

clue.text: Scottish island conceals a new fuel

indicators.note: conceals means the island holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde

explanation.surface: A Scottish island hides a new fuel source.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas burned in lighters and camping stoves, so a fuel.

clue.text: I haul mimosa shrub latterly around island

indicators.note: around means the collected letters are turned the other way
latterly means the final letter of each of those four words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone drags a mimosa bush around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latterly' takes I, L, A, B; 'around' turns them back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indonesian island east of Java, popular with tourists.

clue.text: Staff cover function that incorporates Times Square

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it
a hat is a head covering
tan is the trigonometric tangent function

explanation.surface: Employees cover a role that includes a famous New York square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' is the maths sense: tan, short for tangent.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York borough contains the famous Midtown square; also a whiskey cocktail.

clue.text: Chap used wrong sign language

parts.note: a chap is a man
a cross, X, marks an answer as wrong

explanation.surface: A man used the wrong signing for a sign language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign language' looks like one phrase, but 'sign' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Celtic tongue of the Isle of Man, revived in recent decades.

clue.text: Singer books US city for comeback

indicators.note: for comeback means the combined letters are read from the end

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A singer reserves a US city for a return tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'books' looks like a verb, as in reserving; it is OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice part below soprano, and a singer of that range.

clue.text: Composer ill in bed, endlessly sick

indicators.note: sick means unwell or out of sorts, so the letters are mixed up
endlessly means the last letter of bed is dropped

explanation.surface: A musician lies ill in bed, unable to stop being sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts BED to BE; 'sick' rearranges ILLINBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincenzo Bellini wrote Norma; also a peach and prosecco cocktail.

clue.text: Scorpion's weapon, reversing say, fools solver ultimately

indicators.note: reversing means the say and fools pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
nits are fools, idiots

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of solver

explanation.surface: The setter, Scorpion, gloats that their weapon fools the solver in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns EGNITS into STINGE; the setter's pseudonym is Scorpion.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorpion's tail sting is its weapon; also a brandy cocktail.
